anomalies.observed: The net named RST contains the ground pins (U1.1 GND, U2.4 GND, U3.4 GND, J4.6 GND), the capacitor and pulldown return terminals (C1.2, C2.2, R3.2), and the reset pins of both MCUs (U2.1 ~{RESET}/PB5, U3.1 ~{RESET}/PB5). The reset pins are therefore tied directly to ground, and the reset net is merged with the ground net.
anomalies.expected: The ATtiny reset pins should be pulled up to VCC (through a resistor, and typically via the ISP header), not tied to GND. Ground pins and reset lines should be on separate nets.

evidence.quote: RST : C1.2(passive) C2.2(passive) D1.2(A,passive) J1.4(Pin_4,passive) J1.5(Pin_5,passive) J2.1(Pin_1,passive) J3.3(Pin_3,passive) J4.5(~{RST},passive) J4.6(GND,passive) J5.1(Pin_1,passive) Q2.2(E,passive) R3.2(passive) U1.1(GND,power_in) U2.1(~{RESET}/PB5,bidirectional) U2.4(GND,power_in) U3.1(~{RESET}/PB5,bidirectional) U3.4(GND,power_in)

anomalies.impact: Holding both MCU reset pins at ground keeps the ATtiny chips in permanent reset, so the fan controller firmware never runs. The fan PWM, tach and potentiometer functions would not operate.

anomalies.observed: Two different MCUs (U2 ATtiny45-20P in DIP-8 and U3 ATtiny13V-10S in SOIC-8) are both connected to the same signal nets (PWM, TACH, POT, SCK, SDA, RST, VCC). Both would drive the same pins if populated together.
anomalies.expected: Only one MCU should be populated for the design. If the two parts are alternate footprints, only one should be fitted on a given build.

evidence.quote: PWM : J4.1(MISO,passive) R2.1(passive) R5.2(passive) U2.6(PB1,bidirectional) U3.6(PB1,bidirectional)
TACH : D1.1(K,passive) R4.1(passive) R6.2(passive) U2.3(XTAL2/PB4,bidirectional) U3.3(PB4,bidirectional)

anomalies.impact: If both devices are fitted, two outputs would contend on the same pins and the shared nets would be unreliable. This could cause bus contention and abnormal behaviour.

parsed.summary: The reset pins of both ATtiny MCUs (U2.1 and U3.1) and the ground pins are on the same net named RST, so the reset is tied to ground and the MCUs would be held in reset. The spec describes an unrelated monorepo and does not cover this fan controller, so the verdict rests on standard practice and the netlist.
